items.stem: When picture looks good but audio is poor, audiences generally:

options.text: Do not notice or mind the audio
options.rationale: Audiences are highly sensitive to bad audio.

options.text: Disengage quickly because poor audio is hard to tolerate
options.rationale: Correct: viewers forgive imperfect picture far more than bad sound.

options.text: Prefer the video because it feels authentic
options.rationale: Poor audio reads as low quality, not authentic.

options.text: Watch longer to work out what is said
options.rationale: Straining to hear increases drop-off, not watch time.

items.explanation: Correct: viewers forgive imperfect picture far more than bad sound.

items.stem: The 'rule of thirds' is a guideline for:

options.text: How long each clip should last
options.rationale: That concerns pacing, not the rule of thirds.

options.text: Placing key subjects off-centre for a balanced frame
options.rationale: Correct: the rule of thirds positions subjects along thirds for stronger composition.
Lighting count is unrelated to the rule of thirds.
Export format is a post-production setting.

items.explanation: Correct: the rule of thirds positions subjects along thirds for stronger composition.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in solid pre-production? (Select TWO)

options.text: A script or outline with a clear hook
options.rationale: Correct: a script gives the shoot direction and a strong opening.

options.text: A shot list covering the footage you need
options.rationale: Correct: a shot list ensures you capture the required coverage.

options.text: Deciding to improvise everything on the day
options.rationale: Pure improvisation is the opposite of pre-production.

options.text: Leaving audio and lighting entirely to chance
options.rationale: Planning audio and lighting is part of good pre-production.

items.explanation: Correct: a script gives the shoot direction and a strong opening.; Correct: a shot list ensures you capture the required coverage.
